appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Villeparisis le présente comme «un historien de grande valeur», mais sa première remarque n'est accueillie que par un «Ah !… vous m'en direz tant» dubitatif, et il ne parle que «d'une voix encore si faible que, sauf moi, personne ne l'entendit».
appraisal_events.explanation: Though praised as valuable, the historian is met with polite skepticism and speaks so faintly that almost no one in the salon registers him, exposing a gap between his claimed worth and his marginal social presence.

appraisal_events.evidence: «Elle est vraiment étonnante la petite duchesse... elle leur tenait tête sur la Chine... Vraiment on aurait dit une reine qui tenait le cercle.»
appraisal_events.explanation: D'Argencourt's admiring account elevates the duchesse de Guermantes as the salon's magnetic center, sought out by the most eminent men and likened to a queen holding court.

status_effects.explanation: His speech goes almost entirely unheard in the salon, undercutting the social voice his praised reputation might suggest.
She is portrayed as the magnetic center of elite gatherings, always flanked by the most eminent men present and compared to a reigning queen.
She confidently holds her own in conversation with the German ambassador and M. Deschanel on China, drawing the attention of onlookers.

ambiguities: The historian named 'Pierre' (also called 'l'historien de la Fronde') has no match on the reference sheet and is treated as an unresolved, passage-local character; the speaker of the skeptical '— Ah !… vous m'en direz tant' is also not identified in the passage.
